Q9033.reason: Vienna Convention Article 31(1) requires good-faith interpretation using the ordinary meaning of terms in their context and in light of the treaty's object and purpose, so the shared note's C/D conflicts with the treaty text.

Q9036.reason: A keloid is a firm, raised overgrowth of scar tissue that extends beyond the original wound, so the shared note's C/D does not match.

Q9037.reason: A tracheostomy is most commonly used to aid weaning from prolonged mechanical ventilation, though D (airway security before neck surgery) is also a valid indication, and A is not a standard reason.
